features.title: Kernel (pure Kotlin + TypeScript core)
features.summary: The framework core every app gets: asset registry, engines, runtime state, actions, module system. Pure Kotlin on Android (no Android imports, KMP-ready); framework/core on the web.
capabilities: Hot-swappable assets for every visual slot
Runtime state with persistence of the user's choices
Kernel API level 1 with semver + deprecations

acceptance.text: Compiles with explicit API strict
KernelTest + ConformanceTest pass (7/7)
Compiled in CI on every push
Python port passes the same fixtures

recommendations: Keep the kernel free of Android imports so a Kotlin Multiplatform desktop port stays possible
Bump API_LEVEL only for breaking contract changes; add capabilities instead

history.text: Ported from the web core to Kotlin
First real compile: 0 kernel errors; fixed JS number formatting for conformance

features.title: Asset system (asset@1, 13 core types, open registry)
features.summary: Every visual is a JSON asset (color theme, style theme, layout, menus, toolbar, nav, context menu, dialog, popup, button, slider, container, UAC policy). Ports read the same files; new types register at runtime.
capabilities: Android-only optional types (ui-kit, window, screen-template, icon/string/image/font/motion packs…)

acceptance.text: 41 shared assets validate
Android port loads every shared asset

features.title: Engines: theme, layout, component styles, UAC, context menu, actions
features.summary: Compile assets into tokens and behaviour: theme tokens (core + extended), layouts per window class, component styles, role-based access, context menus per target, action bus with interceptors.

acceptance.text: Theme CSS variables match the reference engine byte for byte
Layouts compile for COMPACT / MEDIUM / EXPANDED

features.title: Porting spec + conformance fixtures
features.summary: framework/spec: PORTING.md plus generated fixtures every port must reproduce exactly (theme vars, layouts, component styles, UAC). The Android kernel passes them.
recommendations: Run the fixtures first when starting the Python port — they define "done" for each engine

features.title: Module system: modules, extension points, services, placeholders
features.summary: Modules register screens, actions, settings, dialogs, services and UI kits through extension points, start in dependency order and can define their own extension points. Placeholders answer NotImplemented until a real module arrives.
capabilities: 20 extension points (routes, actions, settings, dialogs, ui-kits, workers, plugin sources…)
Add modules without rebuilding the kernel

warnings.text: Web port: AxfWebLibrary contract + installLibraries (dependency order, merged views/dialogs/tabs); no extension points or placeholders yet
Python port: Library contract + MemoryKernel stand-in until the kernel is ported

features.title: State, data cache, events, flags, config, migrations
features.summary: AxfStore (reducer/middleware/undo), QueryClient (stale-while-revalidate), EventBus, layered FeatureFlags and Config, migrations ledger + semver.

warnings.text: Web port has the runtime store but not QueryClient / flags / migrations

features.title: Windowing engine: tab groups, floating windows, split, minimize
features.summary: Window schema (types, toolbar rules), tab groups that undock to floating windows, drag tabs between groups and windows, split vertical / horizontal / four-way / custom grid with even distribution (5 → 3+2), minimize to corner title bars (stacked or lined) or a floating toolbar at the cursor, window settings dialog, tree ↔ grid mode.

warnings.text: Divider dragging (split weights) and saved window layouts are suggested follow-ups

screenshots.caption: Compare window: 3 libraries split 2+1, grid view in the top group

features.title: Output terminal
features.summary: One append-only log every install, import, hot swap and kit fallback writes to; auto-scrolling pane as a floating window, dock tab or dialog; follows the console API live over SSE.

screenshots.caption: Output terminal docked in the console

features.title: UI-kit switching + fallback
features.summary: Every component is an abstract kind; the active ui-kit asset picks which library renders it. Kinds a kit lacks fall back to the default AmberX kit and are noted on the output terminal.

warnings.text: Web port renders one kit only — MUI / shadcn / Chakra kits are planned

features.title: Plugin runtime (deliver features after install)
features.summary: plugin@1 manifest, scopes, action macros and a PluginLoader contract exist; loading plugins at runtime is a placeholder.

warnings.text: On Android, plugins can only deliver assets, packs, scripts and macros after install — not compiled code

recommendations: Start with asset packs and action macros downloaded from the console API; they need no code loading

features.title: Background work scheduler
features.summary: WorkSpec / Worker / WorkRegistry contracts and a placeholder scheduler. Real implementation is WorkManager on Android.

features.title: Session, principal, audit log
features.summary: Session/Principal/SessionProvider contracts and an AuditLog service; accounts library uses a mock auth provider.

warnings.text: No real sign-in provider yet

features.title: Android framework modules
features.summary: axf-platform-android, axf-assets, axf-ui (Compose components, kits, element explorer, windows), axf-nav, axf-data, axf-network, axf-devtools, axf-testing. Published as ai.amberx.axf:<module>:0.2.0.

acceptance.text: All modules compile in CI
Published to GitHub Packages
Run on a real device

features.title: Libraries: settings, logging, admin, accounts, profile, billing
features.summary: The six libraries the console and apps build on. Settings and logging are complete; accounts and billing run on mock providers.

android.where: lib-settings, lib-logging, lib-admin, lib-accounts, lib-profile, lib-billing

recommendations: Add the real providers as separate libraries so apps choose them per platform

features.title: Python / PyQt6 port
features.summary: Port the kernel engines to Python, pass the conformance fixtures, add a PyQt6 UI layer, a Qt Widgets kit and a pyqt6 app template.

acceptance.text: Engines pass all fixtures in framework/spec/fixtures
PyQt6 shell renders the shared assets
axf init --template pyqt6

recommendations: Port engines in fixture order: theme → layout → components → UAC
Use dataclasses mirroring the Kotlin models

acceptance.text: CI sweep: every template + 16 boilerplates init and validate

features.title: Library installer + interactive wizard
features.summary: Libraries ship a library.json (params, manifest key, install steps); axf install asks for the parameters and writes manifest, gradle, App.kt and typed <Name>Setup.kt. Also runs at pre-build via --libraries / boilerplate libraries.

features.title: Import third-party UI libraries → AmberX kits
features.summary: axf import-ui clones (git/local) or records (maven/npm) a library, rewrites literals and Material/MUI roles to AXF tokens, saves kit-<id> + its ui-kit asset and applies it to the open project.

warnings.text: The token codemod handles common Compose / MUI / CSS patterns only; untested on a real third-party library
Generated kits keep the default components until overrides are written

recommendations: Try it on Compose Cupertino first and review tokens.map.json

features.title: Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload
features.summary: axf dev watches assets and long-polls changes to devices; the Android HotReloader re-registers changed assets live.

warnings.text: Never tried end to end with a phone

features.title: Library templates (build, port, compile new libraries)
features.summary: Boilerplates for libraries: feature screens, service provider, data feature, device capability, integration, UI kit, background worker, blank — generating Android, web and Python ports, compiling each, and porting a library to another port from its library.json.
capabilities: 8 templates: feature screens, service provider, data feature, device capability, integration, UI kit, background worker, blank
Generate any mix of Android / web / Python ports from one set of parameters
axf compile-library: Gradle (or CI) for Android, tsc for web, compileall + import smoke test for Python
axf port-library: add a missing port later from the library's template
Console: Libraries → Library templates (gallery, wizard, compile and port buttons)

acceptance.text: Every template generates and compiles for web and Python

A real library (e.g. GPS tracker) built from a template and run on a device
